Additionally, Ku-Kak, like the other slaves under Mon's command, was outfitted with an explosive device in his heart programmed to detonate in the instance that Mon died and the Chevin's own heart stopped beating. Although this provided Mon's [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenants]] with the motivation to fight for him, the wampa lacked full awareness of what had been implanted inside him.<ref name="A Mon Alone" />

Mon traveled with an entourage of enslaved creatures wherever he went&mdash;his so-called "zoo"&mdash;to which the wampa belonged. The wampa accompanied Mon during his attack of the [[Almas Sith fortress|Sith fortress]] on the planet [[Almas]] in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]], where the Chevin stole the [[darkstaff]], a powerful Sith artifact, and during which multiple Jedi were killed. A team of Cularin heroes attempting to end the threat that Mon posed encountered Ku-Kak after infiltrating the throne room of Mon's starship, the ''[[Animiasma]]'', within the Cularin asteroid belt.<ref name="A Mon Alone" />

During the Clone Wars, some [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] were known to dress up in special wampa suits for special occasions. For [[Halloween/Legends|Halloween]], a clone trooper was known to have dressed in a [[Purple Fur Wampa Suit|purple fur wampa suit]] and for [[Life Day/Legends|Life Day]] there was a clone trooper that donned a simple white suit.<ref name="CWA">{{TCWA|set=Purple Fur Wampa Suit}}</ref>

===Galactic Civil War and beyond===
{{Quote|That wampa on the wall was my kill!|[[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]]|<ref name="BHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
By [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], among other lethal creatures, including an [[Acklay/Legends|acklay]] and a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]], the Imperial [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Ozzik Sturn]] displayed the head of a wampa in a trophy room he maintained in his personal quarters on the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. Sturn, a big-game hunter, collected the heads of his prey during hunts.<ref name="TFU video game">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

[[File:Wampastuffedanimal.jpg|thumb|right|210px|The [[wampa stuffed animal]]]]
[[0 ABY/Legends|Six months]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Shi'ido [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] shape-shifted into a wampa while he and his nephews, [[Zak Arranda/Legends|Zak Arranda]] and [[Tash Arranda/Legends|Tash Arranda]], were attacked by a horde of [[Zombie/Legends|zombies]] in the [[Crypt of the Ancients]] on the planet [[Necropolis (Core Worlds)|Necropolis]]. Hoole was able to manhandle the zombies in his transformed physicality.<ref name="GOFCOD">''[[Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead]]''</ref> In 1 ABY, Darth Vader and a stormtrooper detail arrived at the [[Jedi Enclave]] on the planet [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], where Vader discovered a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of himself. While the two engaged in a Force duel, a similar clone of Hoole in the transformed shape of a wampa neutralized one of the stormtroopers.<ref name="GOFC">''[[Galaxy of Fear: Clones]]''</ref>

Circa early 3 ABY, [[Crazy Larry's Galactic Getaways]], a travel agency, featured a still image of a wampa in its advertisement for a vacation to Hoth. The advertisement warned potential customers that interaction with the planet's native wildlife occurred at their own risk, citing the wampas' history of attacking landing starships and other vehicles.<ref name="Discover Hoth">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=67957&month=092008|text=Friday Feature &ndash; Discover Hoth!}}</ref>

While in pursuit of the bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] late in 3 ABY, Dash Rendar encountered the Imperial-bioengineered cliff wampa in [[Smuggler's Canyon]] near the [[Cadavine Sector Fleet Imperial Enclave]] on the moon of Gall.<ref name="SOTE" /> [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] encountered the swamp wampas of Dromund Kaas on a mission to that planet in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]].<ref name="JKM" />

Wampas also held an element of cultural significance for many. The forces of the space pirate [[Gir Kybo Ren-Cha]] flew stolen TIE Fighters emblazoned with their trademark red wampa skull signet in the years prior to the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="Tarnoonga">{{DroidsCite|The Pirates of Tarnoonga}}</ref> By [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], [[Holgurn]], a [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] messenger in the employ of Jabba the Hutt, was familiar enough with the creatures to compare the inexperienced Rodian bounty hunter [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]] to the inconspicuousness of a wampa,<ref name="Underworld">''[[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika]]''</ref> while an Imperial [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] [[TIE pilot|pilot]] went by the nickname [["Wampa"/Legends|"Wampa"]] during the Galactic Civil War for icy precision in battle.<ref name="DSII">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Black 11}}</ref> Also during the Galactic Civil War, [[wampa stuffed animal]]s offered denizens the soft and cuddly aspects of the creature without the danger of being mauled and eaten.<ref name="Wampa Stuffed Animal">{{SWGTCG|set=Agents of Deception|cardname=Wampa Stuffed Animal}}</ref>

In later years, [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Gavin Darklighter]] designated an enemy starship as [[Wampa (Yuuzhan Vong warship)|"Wampa"]] during the [[Second Battle of Sernpidal|Battle of Sernpidal]] in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]] amidst the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="Edge of Victory">''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory II: Rebirth]]''</ref> A [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi Initiate]] training clan of the [[New Jedi Order]]&mdash;the [[Wampa Clan]]&mdash;was named after the Hoth creatures.<ref name="Inferno">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref> The martial arts form [[Teräs Käsi/Legends|Teräs Käsi]] consisted of two combat techniques named after the wampa&mdash;the [[Charging Wampa]] and the [[Slashing Wampa]].<ref name="Darth Maul">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> The city of [[Pons Ora/Legends|Pons Ora]] on the planet [[Abafar/Legends|Abafar]] hosted a business known as [[Adopt-a-Wampa/Legends|Adopt-a-Wampa]], though exactly how one could adopt one of these highly dangerous creatures, or why they would want to, was unclear.<ref name="missinginaction">{{TCW|Missing in Action}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|We knew, for instance, of the scene where a wampa actually broke through into Echo Base and mauled a tauntaun&hellip;The wampa filmed in this shot looked absolutely hilarious with a big fluffy face and metallic round eyeballs. We saw the picture in a Kodak shoebox Photo CD Lucasfilm Ltd. provided us with some time ago.|[[Jon Knoles]], discussing [[Lucasfilm]]'s contributions to creating [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'']] for [[Wikipedia:Nintendo 64|Nintendo 64]]|<ref name="LAtakesWampa">{{InsiderCite|33|Wampa Attack!}}</ref>}}
===From concept to creation===
[[File:Wampa_unused_btm.jpg|thumb|left|270px|An early, unused wampa costume design]]
The wampa ice creature was created for [[George Lucas]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and first appeared in [[Donald F. Glut]]'s [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] of the film, just prior to its theatrical debut.<ref name="ESB novel" />

The creature may have been based on the [[Wikipedia:Cryptozoology|cryptozoological]] phenomenon of the "[[Wikipedia:Yeti|Yeti]]," or the "Abominable Snowman," a humanoid beast believed to live in the [[Wikipedia:Himalayas|Himalayas]]. Notes from early concept meetings suggest that the wampa, like the Yeti, may have supernatural powers as well. In early story discussions, the wampa was described as a [[Fish/Legends|fishlike]] beast capable of swimming through the snow,<ref name="BTM" /> and the creatures were intended to be inside the base where the Rebels were hiding, creating chaos when Vader is approaching to begin his attack on the base.<ref name="Annotated Screenplays">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>

In the winter of [[1977]], [[Mark Hamill]] was in a serious car accident that left him in need of reconstructive facial surgery. Many believe that the wampa attack on Skywalker was included in the film to explain Hamill's residual scarring and slightly altered facial features.<ref name="BTM" />

Some of the earliest production drawings of Echo Base's interior from [[May]] [[1978]] include call-outs indicating where a "[[Yuzzem]]" is to break through the ice walls of the base, as seen in ''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back]]''. The concept of the Yuzzem creature was introduced into ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] in [[Alan Dean Foster]]'s novel ''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]'', published on [[March 1]], 1978, before the production drawings were created. This suggests that the creature that came to be known as the wampa was first referred to as a "Yuzzem," until Foster adapted the name for his story.<ref name="ArtofESB">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref><ref name="Splinter">''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]''</ref>

To create the wampa's roar, sound-effects artist [[Randy Thom]] recorded the noises made by an [[Wikipedia:Elephant|elephant]] in the [[Wikipedia:Oakland Zoo|Oakland Zoo]]. Sound designer [[Ben Burtt]] and the film's sound team then recorded the cries of a [[Wikipedia:Sea lion|sea lion]] at [[Wikipedia:Marineland of the Pacific|Marineland of the Pacific]] public oceanarium and mixed that with the elephant recording to produce the final effect.<ref name="Sounds of Star Wars">''[[The Sounds of Star Wars]]''</ref>

===Production struggles===
Originally the wampa was to be portrayed by actor [[Des Webb]] wearing a giant suit<ref name="BTM" /> made of sheepskins<ref name="Master & Apprentice">{{InsiderCite|102|Master & Apprentice (article)}}</ref> on location in [[Wikipedia:Norway|Norway]], where the Hoth scenes were shot. The costume, which required the actor to stand on stilts, proved too unwieldy, and it was too heavy and hot, causing Webb to suffer heat exhaustion. All of the shots of the life-size wampa were eventually cut from the film. Creature designer [[Phil Tippett]] later built a small wampa hand puppet, visible in a quick close-up as the creature attacks Luke Skywalker.<ref name="BTM" />

For the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] release of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' in [[1997]], George Lucas decided to expand the wampa scenes. In order to do so, [[Industrial Light & Magic]] artist [[Howie Weed]] constructed a more mobile version of the costume, without the stilts, which he wore in the film. The new shots were filmed within a scaled-down replica of a cave to create the illusion that the wampa was much larger than a normal Human.<ref name="BTM" />

===Additional scenes===
[[File:Outside_the_Wampa_pen.jpg|thumb|right|250px|C-3PO and R2-D2 view a warning sign on the Echo Base wampa pen in a deleted scene from ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]
Wampas originally played a much more prominent role in early versions of ''The Empire Strikes Back''. In the treatment and the first draft, wampas storm Echo Base shortly before the arrival of the Empire. In the original shooting script, a tauntaun was killed when a wampa stormed into Echo Base. Shots of a wampa breaking through one of the walls of the complex and attacking Rebel soldiers were filmed but ultimately dropped from the final version of the movie. In addition, the wall did not crumble properly and the shot was never successfully achieved. Final versions of the script depicted a mass-coordinated wampa attack on Echo Base. There were several scenes shot for the film that showed this incident, as well as a sequence involving C-3PO tearing a warning sign off the door of a wampa pen, followed by a group of snowtroopers entering the pen only to be attacked by the wampas inside. However, these scenes were later deleted and did not make the final version of the film.<ref name="BTM" />

===Notable appearances===
[[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel's ''Star Wars'']] comic adaptation of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', [[Star Wars (1977) 40|''Star Wars'' (1977) 40]], released in [[October]] [[1980]], was the first ''Star Wars'' source to discuss the deleted wampa scenes in an [[in-universe]] context, in which references are made to the fact that wampas are being held captive at Echo Base.<ref name="Star Wars 40">[[Star Wars (1977) 40|''Star Wars'' (1977) 40]]</ref>

The creature's on-screen ferocity made its appearance in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' a popular candidate for recreation in several [[Star Wars video games|video games]], including [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (1991 video game)|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] for the [[Wikipedia:Nintendo Entertainment System|Nintendo Entertainment System]],<ref name="ESB video game">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (1991 video game)|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' video game (1991)]]</ref> ''[[Super Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' for the [[Wikipedia:Super Nintendo Entertainment System|Super Nintendo Entertainment System]],<ref name="Super Empire Strikes Back" /> ''[[Star Wars Trilogy: Apprentice of the Force]]'' for [[Wikipedia:Game Boy Advance|Game Boy Advance]],<ref name="Apprentice">''[[Star Wars Trilogy: Apprentice of the Force]]''</ref> and ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''.<ref name="LEGO">''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref>

Other releases have sought to expound upon the wampas' attack on Echo Base, depicting their captivity by the Rebels. The [[Wikipedia:Nintendo 64|Nintendo 64]] release of [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'']] was the first visual representation outside of filmed footage to show the wampa pens. The game's designers were specially provided with images of deleted scenes of the wampa by [[Lucasfilm]]<ref name="SWI" /> The subsequent ''[[Star Wars Trilogy Arcade]]'' recreated the escape from Echo Base, in which the player must defeat wampas in an attempt to reach the ''Millennium Falcon''.<ref name="Trilogy Arcade">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Arcade]]''</ref>

===Video games and other appearances===
The wampa has appeared in several other video games. In the [[Wikipedia:Personal computer|computer]] game ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', the wampa is one of many wild creatures that cannot be built or harvested for food, and who will attack any unit it comes near.<ref name="Battlegrounds">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> In ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', a group of wampas battles a variant force of [[Alliance Army/Legends|Rebel infantry]] outside Echo Base on the planet Hoth and also on Rhen Var.<ref name="BFII" /> Wampas can be encountered on Hoth in ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''<ref name="EAW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref> and the expansion ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''.<ref name="FOC">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref> The game [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']] created a new scenario as part of the "Chapter 11: The Battle of Echo Base" expansion module in which wampas, including the giant wampa Unkajo, inhabit a valley outside Echo Base and must be defeated during the Battle of Hoth.<ref name="Galaxies Chapter 11" /><ref name="Secrets of Hoth" />

[[File:MCQ-wampa.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Wampa concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]]]
''LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy'' features an ice-skating wampa, one of several humorous elements interjected into the game.<ref name="LEGO" /> It is possible to play as a wampa and a cliff wampa in the "Escape from Echo Base" and "Gall Spaceport" levels, respectively, in the video game ''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire''.<ref name="SOTE" />

''[[The Star Wars Cookbook: Wookiee Cookies and Other Galactic Recipes]]'' provides a recipe for "Wampa Snow Cones."<ref name="Cookbook">''[[The Star Wars Cookbook: Wookiee Cookies and Other Galactic Recipes]]''</ref>

The Game Boy Advance game ''Star Wars Trilogy: Apprentice of the Force'' depicted Wampas as enemies within the Echo Base level during the Battle of Hoth, one in particular also single-handedly attacking several stormtroopers before focusing its attention on Luke.<ref name="Apprentice" />

===Inconsistencies===
There remains a discrepancy between the nature of the shielded pens that held captive several wampas inside Echo Base, as well as the number of wampas caged. The [[West End Games]] sourcebook [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'']] implies multiple such pens holding several wampas.<ref name="GG3" /> The video game ''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' confirms multiple pens and depicts the wampas as being held behind reinforced cages inside the pens.<ref name="SOTE" /> However, the reference book [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']], which offers an extensively detailed cross-section of the base, includes only one such wampa pen without interior cages. In this small illustration the wampas are seemingly left to roam free within the small pen, while in the close confines of one another.<ref name="SWCL" />

The [[2001]] reference book ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'' and a [[2009]] trading card from the ''[[The Nightsister's Revenge]]'' expansion of the ''[[Star Wars Galaxies Trading Card Game]]''<ref name="TNR Reptomammal Battle" /> stated that wampas are reptomammals,<ref name="Wildlife" /> but the [[2006]] reference book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' states that wampas are primates.<ref name="NEGAS" />

===Non-canon===
The wampa makes several non-canonical appearances.

''[[The Great Golden C-3PO Hunt]]'' tells of the search for the rogue C-3PO following the [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|First Battle of Tatooine]]. During the hunt a group of four stormtroopers are eventually led to Hoth, where an [[Vehicle Command Crewer|Imperial Army pilot]] in the cockpit of an [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transport]] informs them he has seen a wampa, among other things, but no golden droid.<ref name="C-3PO Hunt">''[[The Great Golden C-3PO Hunt]]''</ref>

The wampa makes three non-canonical appearances in the ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'' comic series. The short story "[[Hunger Pains]]" revealed that the wampa that attacked Skywalker did so because her children were hungry,<ref name="Hunger">{{Tales|20|Hunger Pains}}</ref> while Chewbacca retrieves the bracelet of a dead girl from a wampa cave in "[[Ghosts of Hoth]]."<ref name="Ghosts">{{Tales|17|Ghosts of Hoth}}</ref> In "[[The Secret Tales of Luke's Hand!]]," Luke Skywalker's hand, severed in the [[Duel on Cloud City/Legends|duel]] with Darth Vader on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], returns to Hoth to discover the similarly severed arm of the wampa that was maimed by Skywalker. Just as Skywalker had done years before, his hand uses the Force to grab a nearby lightsaber and finishes off the wampa appendage.<ref name="Luke's Hand">{{Tales|8|The Secret Tales of Luke's Hand!}}</ref>

The comic ''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' retells of Skywalker's wampa attack and subsequent escape from the creature's cave; however, he dies on the Hoth wastes before he can be rescued by Han Solo.<ref name="Infinities">''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> Marvel's ''Star Wars'' comic [[Star Wars (1977) 78|''Star Wars'' 78]] describes how pilots [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] and [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]] survived the Battle of Hoth, but were unable to escape and found themselves stranded on the ice planet for months. There, they fended off numerous wampa attacks.<ref name="Hoth Stuff">[[Star Wars (1977) 78|''Star Wars'' (1977) 78]]</ref>

In the young-reader novel ''[[Choose Your Own Star Wars Adventure: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', the reader can opt to let Skywalker die at the hands of the wampa and instead choose to return to Echo Base.<ref name="Choose">''[[Choose Your Own Star Wars Adventure: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>

In the video game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]'', the Emperor's apprentice, Lord [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]], the dark side persona of Galen Marek, encounters many wampas throughout the subterranean ice caverns of Hoth while infiltrating the Rebels' Echo Base during a non-canonical version of the Battle of Hoth. Within the ice caverns, the wampas impede Starkiller's approach by hurling giant balls of ice at him, as well as delivering powerful blows with their claws. Starkiller must also battle his way through several more wampas within the interior of Echo Base itself, where the creatures find themselves the targets of the base's defending Rebel troops as well. The climax of the Echo Base level features a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] between Starkiller and Luke Skywalker. At one point during the duel, Skywalker, having fallen to the ground, uses the Force to break open the sealed door to one of the base's wampa pens, unleashing three of the creatures on Starkiller as a quick diversion. Starkiller must eliminate the freed wampas before pursuing Skywalker. Before finally catching up with Skywalker in Echo Base's main hangar, Starkiller is confronted by several more wampas whom he must dispatch, including another group that burst out of another of the base's holding pens.<ref name="The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]''</ref>

Skywalker encounters wampas as generic enemies on the ice planets of [[Thaldo]], [[Neshtab]], [[Etorasp]], [[Lokondo]], and a fifth unidentified world in the game ''[[Star Wars: Yoda Stories]]''.<ref name="Yoda Stories">''[[Star Wars: Yoda Stories]]''</ref>

====''Star Wars'' (1987 game)====
{{Main|Wampa Vader}}
In the Japanese game released in 1987, a creature who looked like a Wampa possessed shapeshifting abilities, and briefly took the [[Wampa Vader|appearance]] of the Sith Lord Darth Vader. Luke confronted it when trying to rescue his allies on Hoth.
